subject: Green Line Extension and Municipal Policy Updates
overview: Host Danielle Balocca interviewed community advocate Jim Silva regarding the progress of the Green Line Extension, recommendations for city-wide parking reform, and ongoing efforts to initiate a municipal charter review.

items.title: Introduction and Community Background
items.summary: Jim Silva discussed his long-term residency in South Medford and his history founding local organizations like South Medford Residents Together and Safe Medford.

items.title: Local Business Promotion and Shop the Squares
items.summary: Silva highlighted the diversity of local restaurants and the success of the Chamber of Commerce's February 'Shop the Squares' initiative to boost local commerce.

items.title: Green Line Extension Status and Community Liaison Role
items.summary: Silva detailed the history of the Green Line Extension (GLX) and his role as a community liaison advocating for noise mitigation, pedestrian safety, and transit equity.

items.title: Rail Connectivity and Bus Route Advocacy
items.summary: The discussion covered the convenience of the new rail stations for commuters and ongoing advocacy to preserve the 80 bus route for residents who depend on it.

items.title: Parking Policy and Enforcement Reform Recommendations
items.summary: Silva reviewed a sixty-page report submitted to the Mayor that identified parking inequities in South Medford and proposed a more dynamic resident parking program.

items.title: Metered Parking Technology Upgrades
items.summary: The interview addressed the need to replace aging parking kiosks with smart meters or mobile applications and noted the appointment of Faye Morrison as the new parking director.

items.title: Municipal Charter Review Progress and Signature Gathering
items.summary: Silva explained the history of Medford's 1986 charter change and current volunteer efforts to gather five thousand signatures to trigger a formal review process.
